## How fastbrowse works.

fastbrowse lists the page controls, chooses an action, then checks the result.

### Choose from indexed controls

Jev chooses the operation and target in one request from a list of controls on the page. Short factual reads can use Jev as well; the LLM plans the task and reads longer passages.

### Check the result before finishing

Factual answers cite quotes copied from the page. fastbrowse checks those quotes and the task requirements before reporting the task as complete.

### Inspect steps and cost

Each result includes steps, model calls and cost. Compare agents on task success, speed and cost on the benchmarks page.

View benchmarks

## Logins and control.

Reuse a saved local or cloud browser profile, or attach to an existing browser. When a credential is needed, fastbrowse resolves the named secret for its permitted website without putting the value in a prompt.

### Built-in Bitwarden

Resolve logins from the unlocked Bitwarden CLI by their saved website address, including one-time codes when configured.

### Authorization before irreversible actions

fastbrowse asks for approval before actions classified as irreversible. The classifier can miss an irreversible action.

## Choose a browser.

Run hosted, run locally, use a cloud browser, or attach to an existing session.

### Hosted

Once a live-key run starts on fastbrowse hosted, it executes in a sandboxed Chrome on a managed browser pool, with nothing to install. Run it hosted

### Local Chrome

Pass --local to run Chrome on this machine. --headed shows the window, and --profile keeps a signed-in profile on disk.

### Cloud browser

The default is a Browser Use Cloud browser, which passes bot checks a fresh local Chrome can fail. It prints a URL to watch the run live.

### Attach to a browser

Drive a browser that is already running over --cdp-url or --cdp-port , and leave the browser running after the task. --attach takes over an open window, such as an Electron app.

### Cloud extensions

Load up to three ready Browser Use Cloud extensions by ID with cloud_extensions . They are available on a cloud browser only.

### MCP and embedding

fastbrowse-mcp serves one browse tool to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients. The embedding API exposes browser steps, quotes and model spend.

## Use it from your agent.

Install the fastbrowse skill in Codex or Claude Code, then hand your agent a website task. The skill installs instructions only: set the model key and choose a browser as for the CLI. A run is finished only when its status is complete.

### Install the skill

npx skills add agent-labs-dev/fastbrowse --skill fastbrowse

Choose your agent when the installer prompts, then start a new agent session.

## Run a task.

Install the CLI, the Python SDK or the JavaScript SDK, then give fastbrowse a task and a starting page. The JavaScript SDK needs Node.js 20 or newer, and no Python.

# Install uv first; replace ... with your provider keys export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... # for Jev and the LLM that plans and reads # export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=... # optional: use direct TypeSafe for Jev instead # export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... # Jev backup; also serves the LLM when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is unset export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=... # the cloud browser; or pass --local to use Chrome uvx fastbrowse "What is the title of the top story right now?" \ --start https://news.ycombinator.com/ # Without a starting page, fastbrowse proposes the first address from the task uvx fastbrowse "Find the httpx package on PyPI and report its latest released version." # Authorization gates and a secret the model only ever sees by name export SAUCE_PASSWORD=secret_sauce # public practice credential uvx fastbrowse "Log in as standard_user and add the backpack to the cart." \ --start https://www.saucedemo.com/ \ --secret password=SAUCE_PASSWORD \ --authorize # uv tool install fastbrowse # keep fastbrowse on PATH # uv add fastbrowse # or put it in a project

# uv add fastbrowse # Set the OpenRouter key shown in CLI usage; with no browser given, this runs local Chrome. import asyncio from pydantic import BaseModel from fastbrowse import run_task from fastbrowse.models import Limits class Release ( BaseModel ): package: str version: str async def main () -> None : result = await run_task( "Find the httpx package and report its name and latest released version." , start= "https://pypi.org/" , output_schema=Release, limits=Limits(max_dollars= 0.10 ), ) if not result.succeeded: print (result.status, result.error) return release = Release.model_validate(result.data) print (release.package, release.version) for citation in result.citations: print (citation.quote, citation.deep_link) asyncio.run(main())

No Python and no uv on the machine. // The npm package installs the native binary for your platform. // Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment for Jev and the planning LLM. import { Fastbrowse } from 'fastbrowse' ; import { z } from 'zod' ; const Release = z. object ({ package : z. string (), version : z. string () }); const fb = await Fastbrowse . start ({ local : true }); try { const result = await fb. run ( 'Find the httpx package and report its name and latest released version.' , { start : 'https://pypi.org/' , output : Release , limits : { maxDollars : 0.1 }, onEvent : event => { if (event. type === 'step' ) console . error (event. step . operation , event. step . target ); }, signal : AbortSignal . timeout ( 120_000 ), }); console . log (result. status , result. answer ); if (result. status === 'complete' ) console . log (result. output . package , result. output . version ); for ( const evidence of result. evidence ) console . log ( ` " ${evidence.quote} " from ${evidence.url} ` ); } finally { await fb. close (); }

## Run it hosted.

fastbrowse hosted runs the same agent in managed browsers behind an API. Send a task over HTTPS, follow its steps, and pay per run. Keys, secrets, billing and run history live in the console.

### Sandboxed browser pool

Once a live-key run starts, it executes in a sandboxed Chrome on a browser pool that fastbrowse runs on Google Kubernetes Engine. There is no browser to install, update or keep alive.

### Console and API

Sign in at console.fastbrowse.ai to submit runs, follow their steps and see your balance. Your code sends the same runs to api.fastbrowse.ai .

### One request per task

Send a task, and optionally a starting page, to POST /v1/runs at api.fastbrowse.ai . The service runs the browser fleet, model connections, queue and secret store. A test key runs a simulator that returns the same response shapes at no cost.

### Pay per run

A run is priced as a per-run fee plus usage, never below $0.005 . Runs are paid from a balance that your plan's monthly allowance and any top-ups fill. Top up prepaid credits in the console, and the dashboard shows the balance. An allowance does not roll over; a top-up does not expire.

### What a run is charged for

A run is charged when the agent did the work, whatever it proved, including a run that stopped at a sign-in wall or a bot check. A provider outage, an error inside the agent, a cancelled run, a run that expired in the queue and any run made with a test key are not charged.
